W.note: Strongest shopping logic (variant sold-out states, stepper with stock caps, busy/Added/error feedback, focus-trapped drawer that becomes a bottom sheet on mobile), though the blue CTA and gray placeholder glyphs feel template-like and mobile shows only one card per screen.

X.note: Dense five-column grid with search, chips and sort is tidy, but the pastel gradient tiles with initials read as generic placeholders and Add gives only a small 'in cart' note with no variant or quantity control.

Y.note: The most compact design with real product illustrations, clear size chips, sold-out states, steppers, and a bag drawer that restores focus, though the mobile two-column grid leaves an orphaned third card and the size chips wrap awkwardly.

Z.note: Refined editorial cards and an always-visible sticky bag on desktop, but the large square art makes mobile a single tall column and the bag sits below the whole grid on phones, so the cart is hard to reach.
